observations.finding: Treated fields (0.1 and 0.3 uM, 4 fields) are less confluent than DMSO control f_bd4169e2e78f which is a dense monolayer of small uniform cells. Treated cells are larger and more spread with black gaps between cells vs DMSO tight packing. Contrast identical, so real.

DNA/blue: nuclei markedly enlarged vs DMSO. ~25-35% cells have nuclei ~1.5-2x DMSO diameter. Median increase visible. Example f_0388a47df642 center-bottom and f_0018435ead61 center show paired/bilobed large blue masses in one red actin boundary. DMSO nuclei small round uniform.
Nuclei more irregular/elongated, less round. Oval, dumbbell and bilobed forms vs DMSO mostly circular. Paired nuclei suggest binucleation/polyploidy.
Apparent increased integrated DAPI intensity - large nuclei are solid bright blue, filling more area, vs DMSO smaller dimmer blue. At fixed contrast implies more DNA per nucleus.
Overall cell size larger - both cytoplasmic area and long axis expanded vs DMSO compact polygonal cells. Cells appear hypertrophic/spread.
Tubulin/green: perinuclear diffuse microtubule mesh still present, no collapse, no loss of filaments, no obvious mitotic spindle enrichment. Visible in all treated fields similar to DMSO.
F-actin/red: cortical actin at cell periphery still present, stress fibers not lost, no actin aggregates or disruption. No phenotype of actin depolymerization.

notable_cells.why: binucleate cell - two large blue nuclei within single red actin border, example of failed cytokinesis

candidate_mechanisms.why: Strongest match: massive frac_large_nucleus z=80-98, nuc_area z~42, nuc_major_axis z~28, nuc_dna_integrated z=8-13, cell_area/cell_major_axis z=9-12 with decreased solidity/form_factor and increased DNA is classic polyploidy/binucleation from cytokinesis failure with Aurora B inhibition, without primary actin/tubulin disruption. Not microtubule destabilizer/stabilizer - tubulin intact. Consistent across 0.1 and 0.3 uM.

report.uncertainty: moderate - only composites available, no independent channel grayscale to confirm intensity, but morphology strongly polyploid

reflection.text:
This run was scored correct: Aurora kinase inhibitors (p=0.88) matches unblinded AZ258. The phenotype was the driver, not the chemistry.

What got right:
- Phenotype magnitude at low-mid doses was decisive. Wells w_80f45bbd63 (0.1 uM, e5) frac_large_nucleus z=+98.8, nuc_area z=+41.9; w_8b561f0561 (0.3 uM, e2) frac_large_nucleus z=+80.7, nuc_area z=+42.6; w_7d742a2ea2 (1 uM, e4) frac_large_nucleus z=+70.3, nuc_area z=+38.0. These are >70sd shifts in a binucleation/polyploidy readout, consistent with Aurora inhibition leading to cytokinesis failure and large polyploid nuclei PMID 20484572 and mitotic/cytokinetic defects PMID 34406008. I acquired 4 wells spanning 0.1-10 uM after e1 showed 8 doses 0.01-30 uM and 4/4 budget, which sampled onset (e5,e2), plateau (e4) and high-dose (e3).
- Atlas comparison e6 was convergent: NSC 3/4 wells Aurora and k-neighbour 9/10 Aurora vs 1/10 DNA damage. This is an image-based phenotypic screen signal of the type described for Aurora inhibitors PMID 19609559 and reviewed as a screening approach PMID 26779442. The microscopist e10 independently called enlarged irregular nuclei/binucleation with lower density vs DMSO and candidate Aurora on 4 fields, providing orthogonal validation without relying on z-scores alone.
- Calibration to 0.88 was correct. The high-dose well w_b09894f4c4 (10 uM, e3) showed only nuc_area z=+25.2, nuc_major_axis z=+13.5, 203 cells measured vs 421-442 at low doses, and act_glcm_contrast z=+11.4. Dose-response e7 frac_large_nucleus rho=-1.00 (p=0) is non-monotonic decreasing at high dose, e11 cell_count rho=-0.80, and e8 nuc_dna_integrated rho=-0.40 p=0.6 non-significant, indicating cytotoxicity/attrition at 10 uM rather than strengthening polyploidy. Treating e3 as contradicting evidence in hypothesis update e13 prevented overconfidence to 0.95+, as noted in review critique.

What misled or was missed and why:
- The negative rho for frac_large_nucleus e7 could have been read as no dose effect if only the correlation was considered without the well-level magnitudes. Attribution to high-dose cell loss required integrating e3 cell count drop and lower nuc_area vs e2/e5, not the rho alone.
- I did not distinguish Aurora A vs B in this data. Both give large nuclei, but cytokinesis failure/binucleation points to Aurora B. No phospho-Histone H3 Ser10 measurement was acquirable in this budget. The proposed next experiment - phospho-H3 Ser10 IF dose-response vs AZD1152 control and ploidy by flow - is the direct test that was missing.
- Chemistry did not help: e15 lookup AZ258 (CID 59396138) returned no curated ChEMBL mechanisms, from the BBBC021 structure, so mechanism confirmation had to rely entirely on atlas + microscopist. Literature search e16 returned 0 hits for 'Aurora kinase inhibitor polyploidy binucleation enlarged nuclei phenotype' which could have falsely discouraged the call; e17/e18 recovered 1 and 5 hits respectively, sufficient to support the phenotype but not compound-specific.
- Sampling choice: all 4 acquisitions were rep 1; no rep 2, no 0.01 or 0.03 uM to define true EC50 lower bound, and no 30 uM to confirm toxicity ceiling. Budget exhausted 4/4 as noted in review, so this was unavoidable in-run but limits generalizability.

In retrospect, the combination of extreme low-dose large-nucleus z-scores, atlas 9/10 neighbour concordance, and microscopist binucleation with intact cytoskeleton was sufficient, and high-dose discordance was correctly down-weighted. No clinical implications inferred; this is screening data only.
